item.description: This paper addresses the important and challenging task of large-scale unsupervised semantic segmentation (LUSS). item.title: A Multi-View Clustering Approach via Anchoring High-Order Graphs into a Low-Rank Tensor
item.dc:creator: Xi Guo
Hongmei Chen
Biao Xiang
Yong Mi

Chuan Luo

item.description: Graph-based multi-view clustering methods have attracted considerable attention due to their ability to effectively model complex data structures. However, three significant challenges remain: 1) Conventional approaches mainly rely on first-order neighborhood information, making it challenging to capture high-order structural relations among samples. 2) Balancing the consistency and diversity among high-order representations across views remains a key issue. 3) The convex surrogate functions of tensor rank often introduce estimation bias. 4) Existing methods struggle to achieve computational efficiency for both high-dimensional and large-scale datasets. To address these challenges, we propose a novel method, termed A Multi-View Clustering Approach via Anchoring High-Order Graphs into a Low-Rank Tensor (AHLT). AHLT constructs the high-order graphs through cross-view diffusion, enabling samples to capture both intra-view and inter-view high-order neighborhood structures. We also design an anchor-based cross-view propagation strategy for constructing high-order graphs, enabling AHLT to handle both high-dimensional and large-scale datasets efficiently. Furthermore, we integrate high-order graphs and an anchor-based low-rank tensor representation into a unified framework, where the representation tensor is decomposed into a consistency and a heterogeneity component. Tensor nuclear norm constraints and view-specific regularization terms are imposed on these components, respectively, to preserve inter-view diversity while capturing global cross-view correlations. We also design a non-convex tensor nuclear norm to more accurately approximate the true tensor rank. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets verify that AHLT significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. item.description: Estimating camera pose from lines is compelling in structured environments, yet it is difficult when 2D–3D line correspondences are unknown and inherently ambiguous. In the Blind Perspective-n-Line (BPnL) setting studied in prior work, the pose and correspondences must be solved jointly, without any correspondence priors. This difficult problem becomes more challenging due to fragmented detections, repeated and parallel structures, occlusions, and detector noise for the 2D lines in images. As a result, a single 3D scene line may correspond to multiple, or none 2D image lines, yielding 1-to-n correspondence with n ∈ { 0 , 1 , ⋯ } " role="presentation"> n ∈ { 0 , 1 , ⋯ } n ∈ { 0 , 1 , ⋯ } . We address BPnL under this ambiguity by combining imaging geometry with robust correspondence handling using two solvers: (1) the k-start solver performs iterative optimization with multi-start global search to avoid local optima under one-to-many and missing matches. (2) the BPnLNet, a neural network-based solver, estimates soft correspondence probabilities and incorporates them into a geometry-aware objective function, naturally supporting 1-to-n correspondence. item.description: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification remains challenging due to complex spectral–spatial patterns, the growing demand for energy-efficient modeling in resource-constrained remote sensing applications, and the structural limitations of existing graph convolutional network (GCN)- and spiking neural network (SNN)-based methods. Conventional GCNs rely on static graphs and coarse neighborhood aggregation, limiting their ability to model non-Euclidean spectral–spatial relations, while most SNN-based approaches exploit event-driven sparsity for low-energy computation but lack effective adaptive multiscale and structured relational modeling. To address these issues, we propose a multiscale spiking graph convolution aggregation network (MS2GCAN) that integrates spike-driven temporal dynamics with adaptive graph learning. MS2GCAN comprises a multiscale temporal enhancement module for fine-to-coarse spatial encoding, an adaptive spiking graph convolution module with feature-dependent dynamic graphs, and a center spatiotemporal aggregation module for multi-hop spatial fusion with learnable temporal weighting. Experiments on three public hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that MS2GCAN achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with only 0.06M–0.18M parameters. In addition, the proposed model exhibits sparse spiking activity across layers, indicating strong potential for energy-efficient computation. These results validate the effectiveness of MS2GCAN for accurate and resource-efficient HSI classification. The source code will be released at https://github.com/fwx0314/MS2GCAN. item.title: Active Style-Content Dual-Branch Domain Adaptation for Semi-Supervised SAR Object Detection
item.dc:creator: Xi Yang
Quantao Xie
Yirong Yang
Nannan Wang
item.description: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images offer unique advantages in all-weather, all-day remote sensing, but the high acquisition costs and time-consuming annotation processes limit their widespread implementation. Semi-supervised domain adaptation leverages abundant annotated optical images and a small number of labeled SAR images to achieve great performance on SAR images. However, existing semi-supervised domain adaptation object detection methods typically select SAR domain labeled samples randomly, making it difficult to fully exploit the valuable information and distinctive features inherent in the target domain data. Moreover, there is a significant style and content gap between optical and SAR images, and previous methods have not adapted to them in a task-specific manner. To this end, this paper proposes an active style-content dual-branch domain adaptation method specifically designed for semi-supervised object detection in SAR images. The proposed approach employs Task-aware Active Sampling (TAS) module to select the most valuable SAR samples, addressing inefficiencies in random sampling. Also, we employ a dual-branch framework to address the style and content gaps between optical and SAR images. Multi-layer Feature Alignment (MFA) module ensures style alignment by maintaining consistent feature representations across different visual styles, while Gaussian-SAM Image Fusion (G-SIF) module is employed to integrate content from the source domain into the target domain, effectively bridging the gap between optical and SAR images. Extensive experiments on multiple ship and aircraft datasets demonstrate the exceptional generalization capabilities of our proposed model. item.title: A transferable and interpretable approach to slum mapping using building morphometrics and optical imagery
item.dc:creator: Hang Yang
Eunice N. Jimmy
Peter H. Verburg
Monika Kuffer
Alex Levering
Jasper van Vliet
item.description: Slums are defined at the household level by deficiencies in housing and basic services, and their identification is central to understanding and addressing urban deprivation. Previous studies relying on very-high resolution imagery and deep learning method often involve costly data acquisition, intensive computational requirements, and limited transparency in model interpretation. To address these challenges, we propose a building-level slum mapping framework that directly classifies individual buildings using a Random Forest model. The framework leverages explicitly semantic morphometrics from open building footprint data, complemented by spectral, proximity-based, and topographic features, all based on publicly available sources. The model was trained and validated on labeled data from over 250,000 buildings across four major cities in Kenya. Under K-fold cross-validation, the full-feature model achieved strong performance (F1 score = 0.987), compared to 0.836 when using morphological features alone. Spatial cross-validation further demonstrated that combining morphological and spectral features yielded the highest average F1 score (0.742), indicating stable generalization to unseen cities. These findings highlight the value of building-level morphometrics for cost-effective and transferable slum mapping. To support broader applications and reduce the risk of stigmatizing individual households, predicted slum buildings are aggregated into 100-meter grid cells, providing a scalable basis for urban vulnerability assessment and sustainable urban planning. item.description: Building footprint extraction from high-resolution remote sensing images (RSIs) is essential for applications such as urban planning, disaster assessment, and infrastructure management. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each module, confirming the method's effectiveness and efficiency for resource-constrained automatic building extraction tasks. item.title: High-frequency geometry enhanced graph attention network for hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion
item.dc:creator: Ziqing Ma
Chang Yang

item.description: Fusing low-resolution hyperspectral images (LR-HSI) with high-resolution multispectral images (HR-MSI) is essential for hyperspectral image super-resolution, enabling the generation of high-resolution hyperspectral images (HR-HSI) crucial for detailed analysis. Although deep learning methods have advanced this field, many existing approaches focus primarily on deep spatial feature extraction for the recovery of homogeneous regions, often overlooking the explicit modeling of high-frequency geometric features such as edges, corners, curvatures, and other detailed textures. This oversight results in blurred object contours, loss of fine structural details, and spectral distortion, which severely hinders precise analysis in critical HSI applications. To address these limitations, we propose a high-frequency geometry-enhanced graph attention network (GGAT) for hyperspectral and multispectral image (HS-MS) fusion. GGAT effectively restores high-frequency geometric structures in LR-HSI by leveraging nonlocal self-similarity and explicitly modeling high-frequency geometric features. Our approach utilizes image gradients and higher-order derivatives to capture and restore these structures, formulating the task as the joint recovery of the LR-HSI and its spatial derivative images. We decompose LR-HSI and its gradient representations into patches, each forming a graph node. Edges connect query nodes to neighbors, with adaptive weights learned via a graph attention mechanism from HR-MSI to assess neighbor importance. The query node is updated by aggregating these weighted features to explicitly reconstruct high-frequency geometric structures, thereby obtaining HR-HSI with sharp contours, clear detailed structures, and improved spectral fidelity. Experimental results on both simulated and real datasets demonstrate that GGAT significantly outperforms several state-of-the-art techniques in HS-MS fusion, both quantitatively and qualitatively. item.description: Significant progress has been achieved in the applications of multisource datasets, comprising satellite observations, geophysical measurements, geochemical analysis, and geological information, for mineral prospectivity research. However, conventional mineral exploration techniques are increasingly challenged in complex geological settings, especially for deep-seated or concealed deposits, due to their limited capability to integrate and interpret highly heterogeneous multi-source datasets. Deep learning, as a state of the art methodology, can learn joint representations from such heterogeneous Earth observation and geoscientific data, integrate subtle spectral, spatial and structural patterns, and thereby support more efficient and targeted field campaigns by prioritising prospective areas and reducing unnecessary ground surveys. In this systematic review, 349 studies on deep learning for mineral exploration published between 2018 and 2025 are examined. A stage-dependent data framework is proposed to detail how data requirements evolve from regional reconnaissance to deposit-scale targeting. Subsequently, we critically evaluate major deep learning architectures and relate their specific strengths to distinct data characteristics, such as spatial grids, sequences, and graph topologies. Special attention is given to multisource fusion strategies, emphasizing the necessity of rigorous spatial consistency and physical complementarity. Furthermore, persistent challenges limiting operational uptake are identified, including discovery bias in label representativeness, class imbalance, interpretability, and cross-region generalization. Finally, emerging frontiers are discussed, including the role of geospatial foundation models and Large Language Models in automating knowledge extraction. item.description: Deep learning shows significant promise over representation models in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, owing to its data-driven nature for automated feature learning. Meanwhile, compared with the black-box nature of deep learning, representation models offer greater theoretical guarantees and interpretability. To leverage the complementary advantages of both, we formulate the classification task by coupling model-driven with data-driven, and a model knowledge-prior embedded subspace learning network (MKPSL-Net) is presented. Firstly, the low-rank and sparse representation (LRSR) model incorporating deep spatial-spectral integrated dictionary learning (DS 2 IDL) is employed to establish significant subspace prior relationships, where DS 2 IDL learns dictionary atoms in a spatial-spectral self-supervised manner to enhance the subspace representation performance of the model. Secondly, to address the limited capability of LRSR in spatial structure perception and discriminative feature extraction, a contextual information aggregation module (CIAM) is designed to integrate multi-scale features across various receptive field ranges. Thirdly, the proposed subspace prior attention mechanism (SPAM) is utilized to dynamically capture the prior correlations among different subspace components, enhancing the discriminability of the network between inter-class differences. Finally, a composite residual-label joint loss (RLJL) is developed to guide learnable parameters optimization with both residual and label-driven objectives. Experimental results and analyses across four diverse scenarios show that the proposed network exhibits better classification performance than the state-of-the-art methods while exhibiting superior generalization ability. item.description: Historical maps are unique and valuable archives that document geographic features across different time periods. However, automated analysis of historical map images remains a significant challenge due to their wide stylistic variability and the scarcity of annotated training data. For time series, we introduce the annotated Siegfried Building Time Series Dataset and, to reduce annotation costs, propose generating pseudo time series from single-year maps by simulating common temporal transformations. Experimental results show that MapSAM2 learns temporal associations effectively and can accurately segment and link buildings in time series under limited supervision or using pseudo videos. item.description: Recently, there has been considerable advancement in image generation techniques that utilize diffusion models. Pre-trained models like Stable Diffusion leverage strong natural image priors to enhance reconstructed image quality, but their training on natural images creates a data distribution gap with remote sensing images (RSIs), hindering direct transfer. Moreover, current methods for super-resolution in remote sensing that utilize diffusion techniques initiate from random noise and rely on multi-step iterations, leading to high computational costs and noise-induced uncertainty that impairs precise detail recovery. To address these issues, this paper proposes ORDiffSR, an efficient one-step denoising diffusion method for single RSI super-resolution. Using SDXL as the generative prior, it takes low-resolution RSI directly as the diffusion starting point to reduce noise-related uncertainty. To achieve efficient adaptation to complex ground objects and multi-scale features in RSIs, we propose an efficient VAE module and a one-step denoising U-Net network, and adopt LoRA to fine-tune the one-step denoising U-Net network. Furthermore, to maintain the visual fidelity and distribution consistency of the generated outputs, we incorporate a Variational Score Distillation (VSD) loss into the latent space, thereby promoting strong distributional alignment between generated images and authentic high-resolution images. Extensive experiments were conducted on four public RSI datasets, AID, DOTA, DIOR, and WHU-RS19. The results demonstrate that ORDiffSR can accomplish super-resolution reconstruction with a single diffusion step, achieving an inference speed that is over 150 times faster than the EDiffSR method. Meanwhile, it significantly outperforms existing CNN, Transformer, GAN, and diffusion model approaches in terms of both subjective and objective evaluations, providing a novel solution for efficient super-resolution of RSIs. item.description: Recently, Three-dimensional (3D) object detection by fusing light detection and ranging (LiDAR) and camera input has become a new trend. item.description: Vision-and-Language Navigation for UAV (UAV-VLN) requires an agent to autonomously perceive complex environments and navigate based on textual instructions. However, existing methods face two major challenges: the geometric diversity of landmarks in top-down views complicates the recognition of small or narrow objects, and the broad spatial coverage with dense point clouds impedes effective spatial reasoning. To address these issues, we propose DroneNav, a novel two-stage learning paradigm based on a “decouple-then-integrate” design that enhances both performance and interpretability. First, DroneNav constructs a suite of specialized expert models spanning three complementary dimensions: semantic perception, scene-text alignment, and hierarchical decision-making. This reconfigures the navigation pipeline as a expert-driven collaborative framework, facilitating robust navigation through decoupled optimization. To further improve generalization with minimal computational overhead, we introduce an MLLM-Assisted Visual Grounding approach for target refinement and correction, leveraging Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with on-demand activation to enhance scene understanding and mitigate error accumulation from the initial navigation phase, without incurring excessive costs. Extensive experiments on the CityNav benchmark demonstrate that DroneNav significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving the lowest Navigation Error(NE) and the highest Success Rate(SR). Notably, our method reduces the inference time by approximately 49.1% while using 16.4% less computational costs. These results establish DroneNav as a high-performance, interpretable paradigm for UAV navigation in complex environments. The code will be available at https://github.com/mubei1234/DroneNav . item.description: With the rapid growth of unlabeled remote sensing images, supervised learning methods relying on manual annotation have difficulty to meet the demands of large-scale data. Self-supervised contrastive learning provides an effective mechanism to leverage extensive unannotated datasets. However, these methods mainly focus on instance-level discrimination and ignore the underlying clustering distribution. To address this problem, we propose CLIP-Enhanced Contrastive Clustering (CCC), a triple-branch framework designed for remote sensing image retrieval that utilizes the underlying clustering distribution to guide contrastive learning. Specially, CCC proposes a CLIP-based textual branch that constructs auxiliary cluster distributions using only category number, thereby forming a hybrid framework that couples visual contrastive clustering with text-derived semantic priors, eliminating the need for textual descriptions of remote sensing images. item.dc:creator: Feilong Cao
Qiaoyan Qiu

item.description: Point cloud registration aims to accurately align point cloud data from different viewpoints into a unified coordinate system. However, most existing methods struggle to fully exploit the rich semantic information and complex structural features in point clouds during feature extraction, either overemphasizing semantic features or focusing on geometric descriptors without explicitly modeling semantic cues. Additionally, insufficient feature interaction between the source and target point clouds may lead to ambiguous matching. Specifically, a local semantic-structural feature extractor is devised, integrating a self-corrected mechanism and neighbor-aware aggregation to obtain richer local feature descriptors. Next, a bidirectional feature interaction module updates the features of each point by propagating information on a weighted bipartite graph, strengthening the relationships between similar point pairs. By sequentially stacking these two modules, more discriminative features are learned. To enhance the interaction between point clouds during feature matching, a dual-view cooperative Transformer module is presented, combining local and global similarity scores to perceive contextual information. Experiments reveal that SFLMI achieves outstanding performance on public datasets and exhibits acceptable computational efficiency. item.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
item.description: Geospatial foundation models (GFMs), pretrained on massive Earth observations (EO), have emerged as a promising approach to overcoming the limitations in existing featurization methods. Although most studies on GFMs have released the source codes and pre-trained weights, their deployment still demands extensive configuration, environment setup, inference EO preparation, and model fine-tuning. More recently, Google DeepMind has introduced AlphaEarth Foundation (AEF), a GFM pre-trained using multi-source EOs across continuous time. An annual and global embedding dataset is produced using AEF that is ready for analysis and modeling. The internal experiments show that AEF embeddings have outperformed operational models in 15 EO tasks without re-training. However, those experiments are mostly about land cover and land use classification. Applying AEF and other GFMs to agricultural monitoring requires an in-depth evaluation in critical agricultural downstream tasks. There is also a lack of comprehensive comparison between the AEF-based models and traditional remote sensing (RS)-based models under different scenarios, which could offer valuable guidance for researchers and practitioners. This study addresses some of these gaps by evaluating AEF embeddings in three agricultural downstream tasks in the U.S., including crop yield prediction, tillage mapping, and cover crop mapping. Datasets are compiled from both public and private sources to comprehensively evaluate AEF embeddings across tasks at different scales and locations, and RS-based models are trained as comparison models. AEF-based models generally exhibit strong performance on all tasks and are competitive with purpose-built RS-based models in yield prediction and county-level tillage mapping when trained on local data. However, we also find several limitations in current AEF embeddings, such as limited spatial transferability compared to RS-based models, low interpretability, and limited time sensitivity. These limitations suggest exercising caution when applying AEF embeddings in agriculture, where time sensitivity, generalizability, and interpretability is important. To our knowledge, this is the first study that systematically implements and evaluates embeddings from GFMs in agricultural downstream tasks across space, time, and spatial resolutions. The evaluation results and analyses can inform the design of future AEF versions and other GFMs and support their applications in agriculture and Earth science domains. Moreover, the proposed benchmarking workflow and datasets can be readily applied to evaluate future GFMs and facilitate their use in agricultural downstream applications. item.description: Remote sensing video referring object segmentation (RS-RVOS) is challenged by weak target saliency and severe visual information truncation in dynamic scenes, making it extremely difficult to maintain discriminative target representations during segmentation. MQC-SAM introduces a temporal motion consistency module for initial memory calibration, leveraging short-term motion trajectory priors to correct structural deviations and establish accurate memory anchoring. Furthermore, it incorporates a decoupled attention-based memory integration mechanism with dynamic quality assessment, selectively updating high-confidence semantic features while filtering unreliable information, thereby effectively preventing error accumulation and propagation. item.description: Real-world analytics hinges on tabular data, yet prevailing learners face a triple bind: tree ensembles excel on fixed schemas but cannot generalize to new columns, neural nets learn rich features yet overfit small tables, and recent transfer approaches falter when schemas diverge. The LHCC utilizes dual priors to categorize images into light, moderate, or heavy haze conditions, while MCDNet processes the image through a dedicated branch corresponding to the classified haze level. Third, novel DCP and CAP loss functions are incorporated into MCDNet to further enhance dehazing performance. Finally, a haze condition classification loss and a joint training mechanism are proposed to jointly optimize classification accuracy, dehazing performance, and computational efficiency, thereby achieving a superior balance between performance and efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model significantly improves image clarity and color fidelity while maintaining high computational efficiency. Moreover, the modular branch architecture and extensible haze condition classification loss provide excellent scalability, enabling the model to easily accommodate four or more haze conditions.
